topic: Jiraiya raised Nagato as his first 'Child of Prophecy', decades before Naruto was even born, and Naruto inherited the lessons from that loss
title: Jiraiya Chose Nagato Before He Ever Chose Naruto
description:
Decades before Naruto Uzumaki was born, Jiraiya already found a 'Child of Prophecy': a grieving war orphan named Nagato. He trained him for three years, wrote a novel about him, and believed Nagato would bring peace to the world. Here's the full story of Jiraiya's first chosen student, and why losing him shaped everything he later gave Naruto.

From the Rinnegan's first appearance to the night Jiraiya fell trying to save his old student, this traces every chapter connecting Nagato's story to Naruto's name, his forgiveness, and the teacher they ended up sharing.
comment: Was Naruto ever really the Child of Prophecy, or did Jiraiya just get a second chance after Nagato?

lines.text: Jiraiya already had a chosen one decades before Naruto Uzumaki was even born, and his name was Nagato.

shot.fallback: white haired mentor standing beside a quiet orphan boy

lines.text: A prophecy, three years of training, and a book written just for him, all of it happened first.

shot.fallback: traveling ninja receiving an old prophecy

lines.text: So why does almost nobody actually remember that Naruto wasn't even Jiraiya's first real shot at raising the world's savior?

shot.fallback: mentor looking between two different students

lines.text: Jiraiya lost that first student to a war he couldn't stop, no matter how hard he tried.

shot.fallback: mentor grieving over a lost cause

lines.text: And everything good he later gave Naruto was quietly built from that one earlier, painful loss...

shot.fallback: mentor passing something forward to a new student

lines.text: A toad sage on Mount Myoboku once told young Jiraiya exactly what to expect from his future.

shot.fallback: young ninja receiving a prophecy from an ancient toad

lines.text: Somewhere in his travels, Jiraiya would meet the Child of Prophecy, a student who could save the world or ruin it.

shot.fallback: toad sage delivering a grave prediction

lines.text: For years, Jiraiya assumed that student was Minato Namikaze, one of his own genin students, already showing obvious genius.

shot.fallback: young prodigy training under a mentor

lines.text: He trained Minato personally, and even helped shape the technique that became the Rasengan.

shot.fallback: mentor guiding a student's technique

lines.text: It felt like a reasonable guess at the time. Minato really was that talented, even as a kid.

shot.fallback: gifted child showing obvious promise

lines.text: But a prophecy that vague can point at more than one person, and Jiraiya hadn't actually tested it yet.

shot.fallback: uncertain mentor weighing an unclear sign

lines.text: Jiraiya was already a legend by then anyway, feared enough that Konoha offered him the title of Hokage three separate times.

shot.fallback: respected ninja declining a leadership role

lines.text: He turned it down every single time, convinced his own restlessness made him the wrong man for sitting behind a desk.

shot.fallback: wandering ninja preferring the open road

lines.text: That test came later, during a completely different war, in a village that wasn't even his own...

shot.fallback: mentor called away to another conflict

lines.text: During the Second Shinobi World War, Jiraiya, Orochimaru, and Tsunade fought together as Konoha's three Sannin.

shot.fallback: three legendary ninja fighting side by side

lines.text: Chapter 372 is where it actually starts: after one battle near Amegakure, three war orphans approached the Sannin, begging to be taught how to survive.

shot.fallback: three ragged orphans approaching powerful ninja

lines.text: Orochimaru's answer was to offer them a painless way out instead. Jiraiya, guilty over his own role in the war, refused that.

shot.fallback: mentor stepping in to protect orphans

lines.text: He decided to look after the three of them himself: Yahiko, Konan, and a quiet boy named Nagato.

shot.fallback: mentor meeting three young orphans

lines.text: Nagato's own parents were already gone, caught in the crossfire of a war between villages that weren't even his.

shot.fallback: young boy standing alone by a quiet home

lines.text: Grief like that doesn't just disappear. In Nagato, it had already started turning into something else entirely.

shot.fallback: grieving child with a distant, changed look

lines.text: At first, Jiraiya only agreed to feed the three of them and teach them to fish, nothing more.

shot.fallback: mentor providing simple basic survival skills

lines.text: He refused, flatly, to teach them real ninjutsu. War had already taken enough from children his age.

shot.fallback: reluctant mentor withholding dangerous skills

lines.text: Compare that hesitation to how fast Jiraiya would later agree to train Naruto, almost on sight. The caution came from somewhere specific.

shot.search: Jiraiya hesitation then versus Naruto fast
shot.fallback: mentor weighing caution from hard experience

lines.text: So what finally changed his mind about these three particular orphans? Chapter 373 answers that in one single moment.

shot.fallback: mentor's decision point about to shift

lines.text: Jiraiya found out the day an enemy shinobi cornered the orphans, and Nagato's eyes turned red for the first time in front of him.

shot.fallback: young boy's eyes glowing with sudden power

lines.text: Nagato was horrified by what he'd just done, shaking, apologizing to Jiraiya for a power he never asked for.

shot.fallback: frightened child apologizing for sudden power

lines.text: Jiraiya could have scolded him, or worse, feared him the way most adults would have feared a child with eyes like that.

shot.search: Jiraiya chooses not to fear Nagato
shot.fallback: understanding mentor resisting an easy fear

lines.text: Instead he knelt down to Nagato's level and told him the fight was never his fault to begin with.

shot.fallback: mentor kneeling to comfort a frightened child

lines.text: Those eyes were the Rinnegan, a power Jiraiya had only ever heard about in old legend.

shot.fallback: ancient eyes glowing with legendary power

lines.text: He recognized them instantly: the same eyes once used by the Sage of the Six Paths to bring peace to the world.

shot.search: Sage of Six Paths Rinnegan legend
shot.fallback: legendary sage from ancient ninja history

lines.text: Jiraiya told him something he genuinely believed: that pain forces a person to understand others, if they let it.

shot.fallback: mentor offering a difficult, honest comfort

lines.text: That was the moment Jiraiya stopped seeing Nagato as just another orphan to feed and shelter.

shot.fallback: mentor looking at a child with new purpose

lines.text: He decided, right there, that this quiet, grieving boy was the real Child of Prophecy...

shot.fallback: mentor making a life-changing decision

lines.text: So Jiraiya did something he had never once done for Minato: he moved in with Nagato's group and started teaching them everything he knew.

shot.fallback: mentor settling in to raise three orphans

lines.text: For three straight years, on the ground in Amegakure, Jiraiya raised three war orphans like they were his own.

shot.fallback: mentor training children day after day

lines.text: Nagato, because of the Rinnegan, mastered nearly every technique Jiraiya taught him almost instantly.

shot.fallback: gifted student learning advanced jutsu fast

lines.text: Yahiko, meanwhile, was the one with the vision: a dream of a world where orphans like them never had to exist at all.

shot.fallback: passionate young leader sharing a dream

lines.text: Nagato didn't invent that dream. He adopted it from Yahiko, the same way Jiraiya would later adopt it from him.

shot.fallback: dream passing from one believer to another

lines.text: But it wasn't the jutsu that stuck with Jiraiya. It was something Nagato said about ending the fighting around them.

shot.fallback: young boy speaking with quiet conviction

lines.text: Nagato didn't know how yet, but he told Jiraiya he would find a real path to peace someday.

shot.fallback: hopeful child making a quiet vow

lines.text: That one sentence from a child hit Jiraiya hard enough that he started writing a novel about it.

shot.fallback: mentor writing late into the night

lines.text: He called it The Tale of the Utterly Gutsy Shinobi, and when he finally left in chapter 446, he dedicated the finished copy to Nagato by name.

shot.fallback: finished novel dedicated to a young student

lines.text: Years later, Jiraiya would write nothing for Naruto. He didn't need to. He just stayed present instead, which is its own kind of lesson learned.

shot.search: Jiraiya present for Naruto lesson learned
shot.fallback: mentor choosing presence over writing

lines.text: Once the three of them could hold their own against one of Jiraiya's own shadow clones, he decided their training was done.

shot.search: Orphans defeat shadow clone training complete
shot.fallback: students overcoming a difficult final test

lines.text: They formed their own group afterward, calling it Akatsuki, with Yahiko leading and Nagato as its quiet, powerful backbone.

shot.fallback: young leaders founding a new organization

lines.text: Here's the piece most retellings miss completely: Jiraiya never once trained Minato this way, inside an actual war zone, as a surrogate father.

shot.search: Jiraiya unique method Nagato surrogate father
shot.fallback: mentor's rare, deeper method of teaching

lines.text: Minato got lessons after missions. Nagato got a parent showing up every single day for three straight years.

shot.search: Minato lessons versus Nagato daily parent
shot.fallback: two forms of mentorship compared directly

lines.text: Jiraiya walked away from that quiet village confident he had just raised the one person who would fix the whole broken world...

shot.fallback: mentor walking away hopeful for the future

lines.text: Jiraiya's first novel is where Naruto's name actually comes from, and almost no retelling connects the two.

shot.fallback: hidden detail behind a well known story

lines.text: Jiraiya's first novel barely sold at all. He only found real success later, writing very different books under a very different name.

shot.fallback: disappointed author holding unsold books

lines.text: But that first failed novel still found its way to one reader who mattered: a young jonin named Minato Namikaze.

shot.fallback: young ninja reading an old paperback

lines.text: Jiraiya only found real commercial success afterward, writing the very different, much racier Icha Icha novels instead.

shot.fallback: author finding success with different books

lines.text: Those later books made him rich. The first one, the one that actually mattered to Minato, barely broke even.

shot.fallback: modest book overshadowed by later success

lines.text: Minato loved the book's hero so much that he decided to name his own unborn son after him.

shot.search: Minato names unborn son after hero
shot.fallback: expecting father choosing a meaningful name

lines.text: That unborn son was Naruto, named after a character Jiraiya only wrote because of something Nagato once told him.

shot.search: Naruto named after Nagato inspired hero
shot.fallback: newborn connected to an old promise

lines.text: Which means Naruto's own name exists because of Nagato, years before Naruto ever drew a single breath.

shot.fallback: invisible thread connecting two separate lives

lines.text: Jiraiya actually tried to talk them out of it, half-joking that the name would make him the boy's godfather.

shot.fallback: mentor half-jokingly warning the parents

lines.text: Minato and his wife Kushina insisted anyway. They liked the idea of their son being named after a hero who never gave up.

shot.fallback: young couple choosing a hopeful name

lines.text: Jiraiya didn't know any of that yet. As far as he knew, his first chosen one was already out in the world doing exactly what he'd hoped...

shot.fallback: mentor hopeful about a distant student

lines.text: Years passed. Word reached Jiraiya now and then that his old students were doing good work in Amegakure.

shot.fallback: mentor hearing distant news with pride

lines.text: Then one day, that word simply stopped coming, and Jiraiya quietly assumed the worst about all three of them.

shot.fallback: mentor troubled by sudden silence

lines.text: What actually happened was worse than he assumed. Amegakure's old leader, Hanzo, ambushed Yahiko and Nagato together.

shot.fallback: ruthless warlord ambushing two young ninja

lines.text: He held Konan hostage and gave Nagato one impossible choice: turn on Yahiko, or watch Konan suffer instead.

shot.fallback: warlord forcing an impossible decision

lines.text: Yahiko refused to let Nagato carry that choice. He threw himself onto Nagato's own blade before Nagato ever could decide.

shot.fallback: young leader making a final, selfless choice

lines.text: His last words were faith, not fear: that Nagato would still change the world, even after this.

shot.fallback: fading leader expressing unwavering faith

lines.text: Something in Nagato broke that day, and whatever grew back in its place called itself Pain.

shot.fallback: grieving boy transforming into something colder

lines.text: Notice the parallel nobody usually points out: Naruto nearly broke the same way too, the day Jiraiya himself fell.

shot.search: Naruto parallel nearly breaks Jiraiya fall
shot.fallback: young ninja standing at a similar edge

lines.text: The difference is Naruto had Jiraiya's full three years of lessons behind him. Nagato only had three years with no one left to lean on.

shot.fallback: two students facing grief with different support

lines.text: Enraged, Nagato took Konan back and tore through Hanzo's men using a massive statue, though Hanzo himself slipped away.

shot.search: Nagato Demonic Statue tears through forces
shot.fallback: massive statue overwhelming enemy forces

lines.text: Pain and Konan overthrow Hanzo for good in a civil war, and the village starts worshipping Pain as a literal god.

shot.search: Pain Konan overthrow Hanzo civil war
shot.fallback: villagers worshipping a god-like ruler

lines.text: So here's the question that actually matters: if Jiraiya already taught that boy to find a path to peace, how does he end up a god ruling through fear instead?

shot.search: Jiraiya lesson versus Pain fear question
shot.fallback: mentor's old lesson twisted into something else

lines.text: Years later, Jiraiya returns to Amegakure as a spy, hunting the mysterious god now ruling the village from the shadows.

shot.fallback: undercover mentor investigating a hidden ruler

lines.text: He finds Konan first, grown and dangerous, and realizes with a sinking feeling that Pain must be one of his own students.

shot.fallback: mentor recognizing a former student

lines.text: Jiraiya assumes Pain is Nagato specifically, based on nothing more than the Rinnegan he remembers from years ago.

shot.fallback: mentor piecing together an old clue

lines.text: Even disappointed, he still can't bring himself to hate the boy he once knelt down to comfort.

shot.fallback: conflicted mentor unable to feel hatred

lines.text: When he finally faces Pain directly, Jiraiya's disappointment is instant: his chosen one abandoned the path toward peace.

shot.fallback: mentor confronting a fallen student

lines.text: Pain disagrees completely, calling his plan to reshape the world through pain the only righteousness that still makes sense to him.

shot.fallback: masked figure defending a cold philosophy

lines.text: He tells Jiraiya that peace has made Konoha foolish, that people only understand what matters once they've felt real pain themselves.

shot.fallback: cold figure lecturing an old mentor

lines.text: It's a twisted mirror of the exact lesson Jiraiya once gave him as a grieving child about pain teaching understanding.

shot.search: Pain mirrors Jiraiya old lesson twisted
shot.fallback: old wisdom reflected back distorted

lines.text: Jiraiya and Pain fight hard, and for one brief moment Jiraiya actually believes he's won.

shot.fallback: mentor battling a masked figure intensely

lines.text: Then Yahiko's own face appears in front of him, fighting as one of Pain's six bodies, and the whole picture breaks apart.

shot.fallback: familiar face appearing among several bodies

lines.text: Nagato isn't controlling that body in person. He's doing it from somewhere else entirely, hidden and untouched.

shot.fallback: hidden figure directing distant puppets

lines.text: The fight drags Jiraiya under the water, and in his final moments he isn't thinking about Nagato at all anymore.

shot.fallback: mentor sinking beneath dark water

lines.text: He's thinking about Naruto, and for the first time, Jiraiya decides out loud that Naruto might be the real Child of Prophecy instead...

shot.fallback: mentor's last thought turning to a new hope

lines.text: Jiraiya's dying message takes Konoha's entire code team weeks to crack. Only Naruto finally solves it.

shot.fallback: young ninja solving a coded message

lines.text: The message reveals the truth: Pain's six bodies are just puppets. The real mind behind them is Nagato, hidden and alone.

shot.fallback: hidden truth about a puppet master revealed

lines.text: Naruto defeats all six Paths using lessons Jiraiya left behind, then finally meets the man controlling them face to face.

shot.fallback: determined ninja confronting a weakened figure

lines.text: Nagato, weakened and exposed, tells Naruto plainly that he's no longer the same kind child Jiraiya once believed in.

shot.search: Nagato tells Naruto changed kind child
shot.fallback: weary figure admitting how much changed

lines.text: He explains his whole philosophy: short, enforced periods of peace, bought through controlled pain, breaking the endless cycle of hatred.

shot.search: Nagato explains philosophy peace through pain
shot.fallback: weary figure explaining a cold philosophy

lines.text: He wants to settle the score for Jiraiya at first. Just about anyone in his position would.

shot.fallback: furious young ninja seeking justice

lines.text: Then Naruto stops to think about why Jiraiya was fighting in the first place: not for revenge, but for a chance at peace.

shot.fallback: thoughtful ninja reconsidering his anger

lines.text: Instead, Naruto chooses to forgive Nagato, using the exact same belief Jiraiya once wrote into that old, unsold novel.

shot.fallback: compassionate ninja choosing forgiveness instead

lines.text: Nagato realizes the irony immediately: that belief was his own, as a child, long before it was ever Jiraiya's or Naruto's.

shot.fallback: weakened figure recognizing his own old words

lines.text: His own words, handed to Jiraiya, handed to Naruto, now coming back around to reach him one last time.

shot.fallback: full circle of inherited belief completing

lines.text: Nagato even says it out loud: if Jiraiya's story was the first book of a trilogy, his own was just the forgettable middle one.

shot.search: Nagato calls himself middle forgettable volume
shot.fallback: weary figure reflecting on his own role

lines.text: Naruto's story, he says, is the one meant to actually finish what all three of them started decades ago.

shot.fallback: weary figure passing the story forward

lines.text: As atonement, Nagato uses the last of his strength to bring back everyone his attack on Konoha had taken.

shot.fallback: weakened figure performing one final act

lines.text: He tells Naruto he'll go find Jiraiya again, and the two of them will watch Naruto finish what they started.

shot.fallback: peaceful figure looking toward the horizon

lines.text: Even the old toad sage has to admit his original prophecy was wrong in one specific way.

shot.fallback: ancient sage reconsidering an old prediction

lines.text: It was never just one Child of Prophecy. Jiraiya had actually raised two of them, decades apart...

shot.fallback: two separate destinies finally connecting

lines.text: Some people will say Minato was really Jiraiya's first chosen student, since he trained him before any of this.

shot.fallback: mentor and prodigy student training together

lines.text: That's true in one sense. Jiraiya taught Minato real skills, helped build his signature jutsu, believed in his genius early.

shot.fallback: mentor genuinely investing in a gifted student

lines.text: But teaching a prodigy isn't the same as moving into a warzone for three years to personally raise an orphan nobody else wanted.

shot.fallback: mentor making a far deeper commitment

lines.text: That full, parental, life-changing commitment only ever happened once before Naruto, and it happened with Nagato specifically.

shot.search: Parental commitment only Nagato before Naruto
shot.fallback: deep parental bond formed only once

lines.text: It's a small distinction with a huge difference: one is a skill Jiraiya handed down, the other is a wound he spent years carrying.

shot.fallback: two very different legacies compared directly

lines.text: Minato got a talented teacher. Nagato got a father figure willing to rebuild his whole life around one grieving kid's dream.

shot.fallback: two very different kinds of mentorship

lines.text: Even the Great Toad Sage's own prophecy only makes sense once you count Nagato in it alongside Naruto.

shot.search: Toad Sage prophecy counts both students
shot.fallback: ancient sage recognizing two destinies

lines.text: One Child of Prophecy who fell to grief. One who grew up with a mentor already shaped by that exact grief.

shot.search: One child falls one grows from grief
shot.fallback: two parallel destinies shaped by loss

lines.text: Naruto, born after all of this, inherited something neither of them got: a teacher who had already failed once and refused to fail twice.

shot.search: Naruto inherits teacher refusing repeat failure
shot.fallback: determined mentor giving a second chance

lines.text: That's the real reason Jiraiya bought him ice cream, made time for him, treated him like family instead of just a student.

shot.search: Jiraiya ice cream Naruto family treatment
shot.fallback: mentor treating a student like family

lines.text: He'd already learned, the hard way, that a student needs more than training. He needs someone who stays.

shot.fallback: mentor understanding presence over training

lines.text: He wasn't really starting fresh with Naruto at all. He was quietly trying to finish what Nagato's own story ended in tragedy.

shot.fallback: mentor quietly completing an old promise

lines.text: Jiraiya chose Nagato first, loved him like his own son, and lost him to a war neither of them ever started.

shot.search: Jiraiya chose Nagato first loved lost
shot.fallback: mentor's first great love and loss

lines.text: Years later, Obito Uchiha, the man really pulling Akatsuki's strings the whole time, admits defeat in his own strange way.

shot.fallback: masked mastermind reflecting on failure

lines.text: He blames Naruto and Nagato for ruining his entire plan, and since Jiraiya trained them both, Obito calls it Jiraiya's win in the end.

shot.fallback: masked figure crediting an old enemy

lines.text: A man who never became Hokage, who buried one student and barely knew if his last one would survive, still ends up winning the whole war.

shot.fallback: unlikely victor shaping a war's outcome

lines.text: Naruto, years later, tells people that of every shinobi he's ever met, Jiraiya is the one he respects most.

shot.fallback: grateful student honoring an old mentor

lines.text: Not the strongest. Not the smartest. The one who kept trying to raise a savior even after the first attempt went so wrong.

shot.search: Jiraiya respected trying again despite loss
shot.fallback: determined mentor who never gave up

lines.text: That's a harder thing to do than people give him credit for. Most mentors who lose a student that badly just stop teaching entirely.

shot.fallback: rare mentor who kept believing anyway

lines.text: Everything good Naruto got from Jiraiya exists because Nagato broke his heart first.

shot.fallback: two students connected by one broken heart

lines.text: And if you want to see the exact night that heartbreak really started, the ambush in Amegakure, that's the next story in this chain.

shot.fallback: dark village under a stormy sky
